- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast is flat or rising slowly, model tends to underpredict sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for early positive sentiment.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.3) and forecast is rising, model often overestimates rebound; reduce forecast by 1–3% for negative sentiment.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >85), model frequently overcorrects downward; apply a “lag correction” — delay downward shift by 2–3 days and reduce slope.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.7), model often fails to capture mean reversion; add a 1–2% downward bias to forecast if recent 5-day average is above 80.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates downside risk in negative sentiment periods; apply a “sentiment-adjusted floor” — if sentiment < 0.4, cap forecast at 10% below recent 14-day low.
- If sentiment is volatile (fluctuating ±0.2 or more), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior days’ values before projecting.
